notable_absence.finding: This page's own two worked examples use THREE different path stylings for what the HTTP Methods and URIs section calls a single, consistent 'GET /plan' operation: (1) the syntax section's bare `http://$BACKUP_SERVICE_NODE:$BACKUP_SERVICE_PORT/plan`; (2) the first example's `http://127.0.0.1:8097/api/v1/api/v1/plan` - note the DOUBLED `api/v1/api/v1`, which reads as a literal copy-paste bug rather than a documented alternate path, quoted verbatim rather than corrected; and (3) the second example's `http://127.0.0.1:8091/_p/backup/api/v1/plan/PlanBackupMergePrune`, reaching the same operation through the main Cluster Manager port instead of the dedicated Backup Service port. No page in this batch explains the relationship between the direct-port and proxied-through-8091 access paths, or states which is canonical.

cross_component_finding: TWO ACCESS PATHS TO ONE REST API, ONLY ONE OF WHICH THIS BATCH DOCUMENTS ON PURPOSE. backup-get-expired-backups.json and backup-get-repository-info.md both state explicitly that their URIs are 'only available from the Backup Service port (8097 by default) on nodes running the Backup Service' - a direct-port framing. Yet this page's own second example reaches the SAME kind of endpoint (plan info) through port 8091 (already extraction-layer from the analytics/n1ql REST batches) via a `_p/backup/` proxy prefix - the same pattern by which Couchbase Server's main REST port fans out to multiple services' sub-APIs. Read together with backup-get-repository-info.json (file 11, which shows the identical `_p/backup/` pattern for a repository-info call), this is good evidence that the Backup Service REST API is dual-homed: reachable directly on 8097/18091-style dedicated ports AND proxied through the cluster-wide 8091/18091 management port, the same architecture already seen for the Analytics and Query services' REST APIs in earlier rounds (port:8091's own extraction-layer note already lists it serving several such sub-APIs). The 'only available from... 8097' sentence on the other two pages is therefore either an overstatement, or the two access paths differ in what they expose - this batch's own pages do not say which, and I have not resolved it further than recording both facts.
